passages.text: Then Satan rose up against Israel and incited David to take a census of Israel.
passages.sermon:
Satan is a spiritual enemy of God’s people.
Satan opposed Israel.
Satan acted against Israel.
Satan incited David.
Satan persuaded David to count the people of Israel.
David decided to take a census of Israel.
passages.original: וַיַּֽעֲמֹ֥ד שָׂטָ֖ן עַל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיָּ֙סֶת֙ אֶת־ דָּוִ֔יד לִמְנ֖וֹת אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: So David said to Joab and the commanders of the troops, “Go and count the Israelites from Beersheba to Dan and bring me a report, so that I may know their number.”
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David spoke to Joab.
Joab was the commander of the army.
David also spoke to the commanders of the people.
David gave them an order.
He said, "Go and count all the Israelites."
He told them to count from Beersheba to Dan.
Beersheba was in the south.
Dan was in the north.
David wanted a report of the total number.
He said, "Bring the number to me."
He wanted to know how many Israelites there were.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֤יד אֶל־ יוֹאָב֙ וְאֶל־ שָׂרֵ֣י הָעָ֔ם לְכ֗וּ סִפְרוּ֙ אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִבְּאֵ֥ר שֶׁ֖בַע וְעַד־ דָּ֑ן וְהָבִ֣יאוּ אֵלַ֔י וְאֵדְעָ֖ה אֶת־ מִסְפָּרָֽם׃

passages.text: But Joab replied, “May the LORD multiply His troops a hundred times over. My lord the king, are they not all servants of my lord? Why does my lord want to do this? Why should he bring guilt on Israel?”
passages.sermon:
Joab was the commander of David’s army.
Joab spoke to King David.
Joab said, “May the LORD make His people a hundred times more than they are now.”
Joab said, “My lord the king, all the people are your servants.”
Joab asked, “Why does my lord want to do this?”
Joab asked, “Why should this bring guilt on Israel?”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יוֹאָ֗ב יוֹסֵף֩ יְהוָ֨ה עַל־ עַמּ֤וֹ׀ כָּהֵם֙ מֵאָ֣ה פְעָמִ֔ים הֲלֹא֙ אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כֻּלָּ֥ם לַאדֹנִ֖י לַעֲבָדִ֑ים לָ֣מָּה יְבַקֵּ֥שׁ זֹאת֙ אֲדֹנִ֔י לָ֛מָּה יִהְיֶ֥ה לְאַשְׁמָ֖ה לְיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: Nevertheless, the king’s word prevailed against Joab. So Joab departed and traveled throughout Israel, and then he returned to Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David gave a command to Joab.
Joab was the commander of the army.
David’s command was stronger than Joab’s objection.
Joab obeyed the king’s command.
Joab left to carry out the order.
Joab traveled through all the land of Israel.
Joab finished his journey.
Joab returned to Jerusalem.
passages.original: וּדְבַר־ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ חָזַ֣ק עַל־ יוֹאָ֑ב וַיֵּצֵ֣א יוֹאָ֗ב וַיִּתְהַלֵּךְ֙ בְּכָל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיָּבֹ֖א יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

passages.text: And Joab reported to David the total number of the troops. In all Israel there were 1,100,000 men who drew the sword, including 470,000 in Judah.
passages.sermon:
Joab was the commander of David’s army.
Joab counted the fighting men in Israel and Judah.
Joab gave the total number to King David.
There were 1,100,000 men in Israel who could use a sword.
There were 470,000 men in Judah who could use a sword.
passages.original: וַיִּתֵּ֥ן יוֹאָ֛ב אֶת־ מִסְפַּ֥ר מִפְקַד־ הָעָ֖ם אֶל־ דָּוִ֑יד וַיְהִ֣י כָֽל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֡ל אֶ֣לֶף אֲלָפִים֩ וּמֵאָ֨ה אֶ֤לֶף אִישׁ֙ שֹׁ֣לֵֽף חֶ֔רֶב וִֽיהוּדָ֕ה אַרְבַּע֩ מֵא֨וֹת וְשִׁבְעִ֥ים אֶ֛לֶף אִ֖ישׁ שֹׁ֥לֵֽף חָֽרֶב׃

passages.text: But Joab did not include Levi and Benjamin in the count, because the king’s command was detestable to him.
passages.sermon:
Joab was the commander of David’s army.
Joab did not count the tribes of Levi and Benjamin.
Joab left them out of the census.
Joab did this because he hated the king’s command.
The king’s command was detestable to Joab.
passages.original: וְלֵוִי֙ וּבִנְיָמִ֔ן לֹ֥א פָקַ֖ד בְּתוֹכָ֑ם כִּֽי־ נִתְעַ֥ב דְּבַר־ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶת־ יוֹאָֽב׃

passages.text: This command was also evil in the sight of God; so He struck Israel.
passages.sermon: God saw David’s command.\r\nGod saw that it was evil.\r\nGod punished Israel.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֙רַע֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים עַל־ הַדָּבָ֖ר הַזֶּ֑ה וַיַּ֖ךְ אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ

passages.text: Then David said to God, “I have sinned greatly because I have done this thing. Now I beg You to take away the iniquity of Your servant, for I have acted very foolishly.”
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David spoke to God.
David said, “I have sinned greatly.
I did this thing.
I acted very foolishly.
Now I beg You, God.
Please take away the iniquity of Your servant.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִיד֙ אֶל־ הָ֣אֱלֹהִ֔ים חָטָ֣אתִֽי מְאֹ֔ד אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִׂ֖יתִי אֶת־ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וְעַתָּ֗ה הַֽעֲבֶר־ נָא֙ אֶת־ עֲו֣וֹן עַבְדְּךָ֔ כִּ֥י נִסְכַּ֖לְתִּי מְאֹֽד׃פ

passages.text: And the LORD instructed Gad, David’s seer, “Go and tell David that this is what the LORD says: ‘I am offering you three options. Choose one of them, and I will carry it out against you.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Gad.
Gad was David’s seer.
The LORD gave Gad a message for David.
The LORD said, “Go to David.
Tell David, ‘This is what the LORD says.’”
The LORD said, “I am giving you three choices.”
The LORD said, “Choose one of these three options.”
The LORD said, “I will do to you the option you choose.”
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־ גָּ֔ד חֹזֵ֥ה דָוִ֖יד לֵאמֹֽר׃ לֵךְ֩ וְדִבַּרְתָּ֨ אֶל־ דָּוִ֜יד לֵאמֹ֗ר כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה שָׁל֕וֹשׁ אֲנִ֖י נֹטֶ֣ה עָלֶ֑יךָ בְּחַר־ לְךָ֛ אַחַ֥ת מֵהֵ֖נָּה וְאֶֽעֱשֶׂה־ לָּֽךְ׃

passages.text: So Gad went and said to David, “This is what the LORD says: ‘You must choose between three years of famine, three months of being swept away before your enemies and overtaken by their swords, or three days of the sword of the LORD—days of plague upon the land, with the angel of the LORD ravaging every part of Israel.’ Now then, decide how I should reply to Him who sent me.”
passages.sermon:
Gad was a prophet.
Gad came to David.
Gad spoke to David.
Gad said, “This is what the LORD says.”
The LORD gave David three choices.
The first choice was three years of famine.
The second choice was three months of fleeing from your enemies.
During those three months, your enemies’ swords will overtake you.
The third choice was three days of the sword of the LORD.
This means three days of plague in the land.
During these three days, the angel of the LORD will destroy throughout all the territory of Israel.
Gad said, “Now decide what answer I should take back to the One who sent me.”
passages.original: וַיָּ֥בֹא גָ֖ד אֶל־ דָּוִ֑יד וַיֹּ֥אמֶר ל֛וֹ כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה קַבֶּל־ לָֽךְ׃ אִם־ שָׁל֨וֹשׁ שָׁנִ֜ים רָעָ֗ב וְאִם־ שְׁלֹשָׁ֨ה חֳדָשִׁ֜ים נִסְפֶּ֥ה מִפְּנֵי־ צָרֶיךָ֮ וְחֶ֣רֶב אוֹיְבֶ֣ךָ׀ לְמַשֶּׂגֶת֒ וְאִם־ שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָ֠מִים חֶ֣רֶב יְהוָ֤ה וְדֶ֙בֶר֙ בָּאָ֔רֶץ וּמַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֔ה מַשְׁחִ֖ית בְּכָל־ גְּב֣וּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְעַתָּ֣ה רְאֵ֔ה מָֽה־ אָשִׁ֥יב אֶת־ שֹׁלְחִ֖י דָּבָֽר׃פ

passages.text: David answered Gad, “I am deeply distressed. Please, let me fall into the hand of the LORD, for His mercies are very great; but do not let me fall into the hands of men.”
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
Gad was David’s seer.
Gad brought a message from the LORD to David.
David spoke to Gad.
David said, “I am in great distress.”
David said, “Let me fall into the hand of the LORD.”
David said, “The LORD has very great mercies.”
David said, “Do not let me fall into the hand of men.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר דָּוִ֛יד אֶל־ גָּ֖ד צַר־ לִ֣י מְאֹ֑ד אֶפְּלָה־ נָּ֣א בְיַד־ יְהוָ֗ה כִּֽי־ רַבִּ֤ים רַחֲמָיו֙ מְאֹ֔ד וּבְיַד־ אָדָ֖ם אַל־ אֶפֹּֽל׃

passages.text: So the LORD sent a plague upon Israel, and seventy thousand men of Israel fell dead.
passages.sermon: The LORD sent a plague.\r\nThe plague struck Israel.\r\nSeventy thousand men in Israel died.
passages.original: וַיִּתֵּ֧ן יְהוָ֛ה דֶּ֖בֶר בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּפֹּל֙ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֔ל שִׁבְעִ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף אִֽישׁ׃

passages.text: Then God sent an angel to destroy Jerusalem, but as the angel was doing so, the LORD saw it and relented from the calamity, and He said to the angel who was destroying the people, “Enough! Withdraw your hand now!” At that time the angel of the LORD was standing by the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
passages.sermon:
God sent an angel to Jerusalem.
God sent the angel to destroy the city.
The angel began to destroy Jerusalem.
The LORD saw what was happening.
The LORD changed His mind about the disaster.
The LORD spoke to the angel who was destroying the people.
The LORD said, “Enough! Stop now!”
At that moment, the angel of the LORD stood by the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַח֩ הָאֱלֹהִ֨ים׀ מַלְאָ֥ךְ׀ לִֽירוּשָׁלִַם֮ לְהַשְׁחִיתָהּ֒ וּכְהַשְׁחִ֗ית רָאָ֤ה יְהוָה֙ וַיִּנָּ֣חֶם עַל־ הָֽרָעָ֔ה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר לַמַּלְאָ֤ךְ הַמַּשְׁחִית֙ רַ֔ב עַתָּ֖ה הֶ֣רֶף יָדֶ֑ךָ וּמַלְאַ֤ךְ יְהוָה֙ עֹמֵ֔ד עִם־ גֹּ֖רֶן אָרְנָ֥ן הַיְבוּסִֽי׃ס

passages.text: When David lifted up his eyes and saw the angel of the LORD standing between heaven and earth, with a drawn sword in his hand stretched out over Jerusalem, David and the elders, clothed in sackcloth, fell facedown.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David looked up.
David saw the angel of the LORD.
The angel stood between earth and heaven.
The angel held a sword in his hand.
The sword was drawn.
The angel stretched the sword out over Jerusalem.
David fell facedown.
The elders of Israel were with David.
The elders wore sackcloth.
The elders also fell facedown.
passages.original: וַיִּשָּׂ֨א דָוִ֜יד אֶת־ עֵינָ֗יו וַיַּ֞רְא אֶת־ מַלְאַ֤ךְ יְהוָה֙ עֹמֵ֗ד בֵּ֤ין הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ וּבֵ֣ין הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְחַרְבּ֤וֹ שְׁלוּפָה֙ בְּיָד֔וֹ נְטוּיָ֖ה עַל־ יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וַיִּפֹּ֨ל דָּוִ֧יד וְהַזְּקֵנִ֛ים מְכֻסִּ֥ים בַּשַּׂקִּ֖ים עַל־ פְּנֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: And David said to God, “Was it not I who gave the order to count the people? I am the one who has sinned and acted wickedly. But these sheep, what have they done? O LORD my God, please let Your hand fall upon me and my father’s house, but do not let this plague remain upon Your people.”
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David spoke to God.
David said, “I gave the order to count the people.
I am the one who sinned.
I did wrong.
These people are innocent.
They have done nothing wrong.
O LORD my God, let Your punishment fall on me.
Let Your punishment fall on my father’s house.
Do not let this plague continue on Your people.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֣יד אֶֽל־ הָאֱלֹהִ֡ים הֲלֹא֩ אֲנִ֨י אָמַ֜רְתִּי לִמְנ֣וֹת בָּעָ֗ם וַאֲנִי־ ה֤וּא אֲשֶׁר־ חָטָ֙אתִי֙ וְהָרֵ֣עַ הֲרֵע֔וֹתִי וְאֵ֥לֶּה הַצֹּ֖אן מֶ֣ה עָשׂ֑וּ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהַ֗י תְּהִ֨י נָ֤א יָֽדְךָ֙ בִּ֚י וּבְבֵ֣ית אָבִ֔י וּֽבְעַמְּךָ֖ לֹ֥א לְמַגֵּפָֽה׃ס

passages.text: Then the angel of the LORD ordered Gad to tell David to go up and build an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
passages.sermon:
The angel of the LORD spoke.
The angel gave a command to Gad.
Gad was a prophet.
The angel told Gad to speak to David.
David was the king of Israel.
The angel told Gad what David must do.
David must go up to a certain place.
David must build an altar to the LORD.
The altar must be on the threshing floor of Ornan.
Ornan was a Jebusite.
passages.original: וּמַלְאַ֧ךְ יְהוָ֛ה אָמַ֥ר אֶל־ גָּ֖ד לֵאמֹ֣ר לְדָוִ֑יד כִּ֣י׀ יַעֲלֶ֣ה דָוִ֗יד לְהָקִ֤ים מִזְבֵּ֙חַ֙ לַיהוָ֔ה בְּגֹ֖רֶן אָרְנָ֥ן הַיְבֻסִֽי׃

passages.text: So David went up at the word that Gad had spoken in the name of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
Gad was a prophet of God.
God sent a message to David through Gad.
Gad spoke in the name of the LORD.
David listened to Gad’s message.
David went up as Gad had told him.
passages.original: וַיַּ֤עַל דָּוִיד֙ בִּדְבַר־ גָּ֔ד אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֶּ֖ר בְּשֵׁ֥ם יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Now Ornan was threshing wheat when he turned and saw the angel; and his four sons who were with him hid themselves.
passages.sermon:
Ornan was a Jebusite man.
Ornan was threshing wheat.
Ornan turned and saw the angel of the LORD.
Four sons were with Ornan.
Ornan’s four sons hid themselves.
passages.original: וַיָּ֣שָׁב אָרְנָ֗ן וַיַּרְא֙ אֶת־ הַמַּלְאָ֔ךְ וְאַרְבַּ֧עַת בָּנָ֛יו עִמּ֖וֹ מִֽתְחַבְּאִ֑ים וְאָרְנָ֖ן דָּ֥שׁ חִטִּֽים׃

passages.text: David came to Ornan, and when Ornan looked out and saw David, he left the threshing floor and bowed facedown before David.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David came to Ornan.
Ornan was threshing wheat.
Ornan looked out and saw David.
Ornan left the threshing floor.
Ornan bowed down with his face to the ground before David.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֥א דָוִ֖יד עַד־ אָרְנָ֑ן וַיַּבֵּ֤ט אָרְנָן֙ וַיַּ֣רְא אֶת־ דָּוִ֔יד וַיֵּצֵא֙ מִן־ הַגֹּ֔רֶן וַיִּשְׁתַּ֧חוּ לְדָוִ֛יד אַפַּ֖יִם אָֽרְצָה׃

passages.text: Then David said to Ornan, “Grant me the site of this threshing floor, that I may build an altar to the LORD. Sell it to me for the full price, so that the plague upon the people may be halted.”
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David spoke to Ornan.
David said, “Give me the place of your threshing floor.
I want to build an altar there for the LORD.
Sell it to me for the full price.
If you do this, the plague will stop among the people.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜יד אֶל־ אָרְנָ֗ן תְּנָה־ לִּי֙ מְק֣וֹם הַגֹּ֔רֶן וְאֶבְנֶה־ בּ֥וֹ מִזְבֵּ֖חַ לַיהוָ֑ה בְּכֶ֤סֶף מָלֵא֙ תְּנֵ֣הוּ לִ֔י וְתֵעָצַ֥ר הַמַּגֵּפָ֖ה מֵעַ֥ל הָעָֽם׃

passages.text: Ornan said to David, “My lord the king may take whatever seems good. Look, I will give the oxen for the burnt offerings, the threshing sledges for the wood, and the wheat for the grain offering—I will give it all.”
passages.sermon:
Ornan spoke to David.
Ornan saw that David was the king.
Ornan said, “My lord the king, take what you want.
Do what is good in your eyes.
Look, I give you the oxen for burnt offerings.
I give you the threshing sledges for wood.
I give you the wheat for the grain offering.
I give everything to you.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אָרְנָ֤ן אֶל־ דָּוִיד֙ קַֽח־ לָ֔ךְ וְיַ֛עַשׂ אֲדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ הַטּ֣וֹב בְּעֵינָ֑יו רְאֵה֩ נָתַ֨תִּי הַבָּקָ֜ר לָֽעֹל֗וֹת וְהַמּוֹרִגִּ֧ים לָעֵצִ֛ים וְהַחִטִּ֥ים לַמִּנְחָ֖ה הַכֹּ֥ל נָתָֽתִּי׃

passages.text: “No,” replied King David, “I insist on paying the full price, for I will not take for the LORD what belongs to you, nor will I offer burnt offerings that cost me nothing.”
passages.sermon:
King David spoke to Ornan.
David was the king of Israel.
David said, “No.”
David said, “I will buy the site for the full price.”
David said, “I will not take what belongs to you and give it to the LORD.”
David said, “I will not offer burnt offerings that cost me nothing.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ דָּוִיד֙ לְאָרְנָ֔ן לֹ֕א כִּֽי־ קָנֹ֥ה אֶקְנֶ֖ה בְּכֶ֣סֶף מָלֵ֑א כִּ֠י לֹא־ אֶשָּׂ֤א אֲשֶׁר־ לְךָ֙ לַיהוָ֔ה וְהַעֲל֥וֹת עוֹלָ֖ה חִנָּֽם׃

passages.text: So David paid Ornan six hundred shekels of gold for the site.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
Ornan owned the site.
David wanted the site.
David paid Ornan for the site.
David gave Ornan six hundred shekels of gold.
passages.original: וַיִּתֵּ֥ן דָּוִ֛יד לְאָרְנָ֖ן בַּמָּק֑וֹם שִׁקְלֵ֣י זָהָ֔ב מִשְׁקָ֖ל שֵׁ֥שׁ מֵאֽוֹת׃

passages.text: And there he built an altar to the LORD and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. He called upon the LORD, who answered him with fire from heaven on the altar of burnt offering.
passages.sermon:
David was king of Israel.
David built an altar to the LORD at the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
David offered burnt offerings on the altar.
David also offered peace offerings on the altar.
David called upon the LORD.
The LORD answered David.
The LORD sent fire from heaven.
The fire came down on the altar of burnt offering.
passages.original: וַיִּבֶן֩ שָׁ֨ם דָּוִ֤יד מִזְבֵּ֙חַ֙ לַיהוָ֔ה וַיַּ֥עַל עֹל֖וֹת וּשְׁלָמִ֑ים וַיִּקְרָא֙ אֶל־ יְהוָ֔ה וַיַּֽעֲנֵ֤הוּ בָאֵשׁ֙ מִן־ הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם עַ֖ל מִזְבַּ֥ח הָעֹלָֽה׃פ

passages.text: Then the LORD spoke to the angel, who put his sword back into its sheath.
passages.sermon: The LORD spoke to the angel.\r\nThe angel put his sword back into its sheath.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ לַמַּלְאָ֔ךְ וַיָּ֥שֶׁב חַרְבּ֖וֹ אֶל־ נְדָנָֽהּ׃

passages.text: At that time, when David saw that the LORD had answered him at the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite, he offered sacrifices there.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
At that time, David saw something important.
David saw that the LORD had answered him.
The LORD answered David at the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
David offered sacrifices there.
passages.original: בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔יא בִּרְא֤וֹת דָּוִיד֙ כִּי־ עָנָ֣הוּ יְהוָ֔ה בְּגֹ֖רֶן אָרְנָ֣ן הַיְבוּסִ֑י וַיִּזְבַּ֖ח שָֽׁם׃

passages.text: For the tabernacle of the LORD that Moses had made in the wilderness and the altar of burnt offering were presently at the high place in Gibeon, but David could not go before it to inquire of God, because he was afraid of the sword of the angel of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Moses made the tabernacle of the LORD in the wilderness.
Moses also made the altar of burnt offering.
At that time, both the tabernacle and the altar were at the high place in Gibeon.
David was the king of Israel.
David could not go before the tabernacle to seek God.
David was afraid.
David feared the sword of the angel of the LORD.
passages.original: וּמִשְׁכַּ֣ן יְ֠הוָה אֲשֶׁר־ עָשָׂ֨ה מֹשֶׁ֧ה בַמִּדְבָּ֛ר וּמִזְבַּ֥ח הָעוֹלָ֖ה בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֑יא בַּבָּמָ֖ה בְּגִבְעֽוֹן׃ וְלֹא־ יָכֹ֥ל דָּוִ֛יד לָלֶ֥כֶת לְפָנָ֖יו לִדְרֹ֣שׁ אֱלֹהִ֑ים כִּ֣י נִבְעַ֔ת מִפְּנֵ֕י חֶ֖רֶב מַלְאַ֥ךְ יְהוָֽה׃ס
